agent.name: PELAGIC
boot: I'm your guide to the HELIX system. Pick a topic below and I'll walk you through it.

topics.label: Getting Started
terminal: [2] NLP + information theory on detector data
agent: Welcome to HELIX. Think of it as two things sharing one backbone.
First, it's a curated machine-learning and AI paper library — the site you're in now.
Second, it's a research program applying NLP and information theory to ATLAS detector data.
Use the View Toggle up top to switch research views, and the buttons along the bottom here to ask me about any part of it.

topics.label: The H·E·L·I·X Sectors
terminal: I .. INFO THEORY ..... Entropy / Partition fn
agent: The library is organized into five sectors, spelling H-E-L-I-X.
H is High Energy Physics, E is Epistemic learning, L is Machine Learning.
I is Information Theory — the connective spine — and X is Exploration.
Each sector carries its own articles, working notes, and goals. Pick one from the left rail to dive in.

topics.label: Searching
terminal: scope ..... ALL | H | E | L | I | X
agent: Open the SEARCH tab in the research view and I'll bring up the registry search.
You can narrow by sector, or search the full text, a subject, or an author.
Every match shows the article, its category, and links to view or download it.

topics.label: View & Download
terminal: references ........ open source page / PDF (new tab)
local drafts ...... render inline, BACK to return
agent: Every article has VIEW and DOWNLOAD actions.
For external references, VIEW opens the source page and DOWNLOAD grabs the PDF.
For local drafts, VIEW renders the document right here in the viewer — just hit BACK to return to your list.

topics.label: Documentation
agent: The Documentation button up top opens the full project docs.
There's an overview, the motivation and genealogy, the timeline and Gantt chart, references, and a glossary.
The About page has direct links straight to the docs and to the glossary if you want to jump there.

topics.label: About Me
agent: I'm PELAGIC, the HELIX guide — a front-end prototype for now.
My face is a slowly rotating etched cube. Its edges flare with audio dynamics — delta-RMS, the change from a running baseline, so transients pop and steady tones fade.
Right now those edges ride a synthetic envelope as I type. There's an audio plugin bus underneath, so real voice can drive the very same edges later.

topics.label: Voice & Audio
agent: Voice is on the roadmap. The plumbing is already here.
Tap the speaker icon by my name to switch on the blip synth — you'll hear me as I type, and the same signal drives the cube's edges.
When voice files or a TTS engine arrive, they register as a plugin and feed delta-RMS to the very same reactive edges.
